title: Error-space geometry and positivity orders of encoded reduction maps
abstract: We study tensor products of reduction maps after restriction to perfect-tensor encodings. An error-support expansion of the unnormalized Choi matrix accommodates multiple logical reference parties and arbitrary complex absolutely maximally entangled states. For one logical party, odd physical length n and 0<t<=1, averaging orthogonal error families over fixed-size site subsets gives a completely positive output complement under the sufficient condition d>=2n/t. The encoded map then has an exact Schmidt-rank sign criterion and optimal dimension-uniform positivity order floor(t^(-n)). At t=1/2, a separate estimate covers d>=2n. For two logical parties and four physical outputs, the half-parameter map is completely positive exactly in the admissible dimensions 2<=d<=12. In dimensions d>=13 it is not completely positive, but is k-positive at least through floor(2d(d-2)/(d-6)). Explicit polynomial-evaluation codes give failure at rank9d for every prime d>=43, establishing linear growth up to unmatched constants for those examples. Code existence, the Schmidt-overlap criterion and the reduction-map family are prior ingredients. The results retain substantive code-support restrictions and belong to the completely copositive class.
